summary: The study reports the synthesis and characterization of indium tris-guanidinate complexes as precursors for water-assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD) of In2O3 thin films. The ALD process was optimized with a temperature range of 230–300 °C, resulting in high-quality, uniform In2O3 films with good optical transparency and self-limiting growth characteristics.
evidence: As shown in Fig. 2b, the In2O3 film growth rate dependence was studied in the temperature range of 150 –350 °C. A surface saturated growth and a well-defined ALD window were observed in the temperature range of 230 –300 °C with a growth per cycle (GPC) of 0.4 –0.45 Å. The ALD process was self-limiting with a well-defined ALD window in the temperature range of 230 –300 °C.
